name: Copeland
desc: Makes compressors, controls and software for heating, cooling and refrigeration used in HVAC and cold chain systems worldwide.
markets: Sells to equipment makers and contractors worldwide; manufacturing in the US and other regions; no specific new expansion plans known.
rationale: B2B component maker with low consumer awareness; hospitality and technology showcase could suit, but marketing culture is limited.
changed: Sold by Emerson to Blackstone in 2023 (Emerson kept a minority stake)

name: Foxconn Technology Group
desc: Taiwanese contract electronics manufacturer, formally Hon Hai Precision Industry, assembling smartphones, servers and electric vehicles for other brands.
markets: Plants in China, India, Vietnam, Mexico and the US; customers include Apple and Nvidia; expanding in AI servers and EVs.
rationale: Global scale and EV and AI ambitions give a technology showcase and hospitality case, but it is a B2B brand.

name: LG Display
desc: Korean maker of OLED and LCD display panels for televisions, smartphones, monitors, laptops and cars.
markets: Supplies LG Electronics, Apple and automotive customers; plants in South Korea, China, Vietnam and Poland.
rationale: Automotive display push suits a technology showcase with F1-linked carmakers, but it is a B2B component supplier.

name: AT&S
desc: Austrian maker of high-end printed circuit boards and IC substrates for smartphones, servers, AI chips and cars.
industry: circuit board and IC substrate maker
markets: Plants in Austria, China, India and Malaysia; customers are major chip and electronics firms in Europe, Asia and the US.
rationale: B2B supplier with little consumer profile; limited marketing culture, though an Austrian tech hospitality angle exists.

name: Columbus McKinnon
desc: Designs and makes hoists, cranes, chain, rigging and motion control lifting equipment for industrial, entertainment and construction customers.
markets: Sells in North America, Europe and Asia; entertainment rigging used at live events; no specific expansion plans known.
rationale: Event rigging and lifting business links to live-event infrastructure, but it is a B2B industrial brand with modest marketing.

name: Viavi Solutions
desc: Makes network test and measurement equipment for telecom carriers and data centers, plus optical security coatings for banknotes.
markets: Customers are telecom carriers, data centers and cable operators across the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Telecom and data-centre buyers suit B2B hospitality and a network-reliability showcase, though brand marketing spend is modest.

name: Diodes Incorporated
desc: Designs and supplies discrete, analog and mixed-signal semiconductors for automotive, industrial, computing, communications and consumer markets.
markets: Manufacturing and sales in the US, Asia and Europe; customers are electronics and automotive makers worldwide.
rationale: Automotive chip supply gives a technology tie-in, but it is a B2B component brand with limited consumer reach.

name: Texas Instruments
desc: Designs and manufactures analog and embedded processing semiconductors and calculators for industrial, automotive, personal electronics and communications customers.
markets: Sells to tens of thousands of customers worldwide; building new US fabs; calculators sold through education channels.
rationale: Large chipmaker with automotive and industrial customers; technology showcase and B2B hospitality fit, though it rarely sponsors sport.

name: Advanced Vision Semiconductor Manufacturing
desc: Semiconductor manufacturing company based in Koshi, Japan, per Crunchbase; products, owners and customers are not confirmed.
markets: Based in Japan; no confirmed customers, owners or expansion plans.
rationale: Unverified chip-manufacturing entity with no known brand activity; weak F1 fit until more is known.

name: AMETEK
desc: Manufactures electronic instruments and electromechanical devices, including sensors, motors and precision instrumentation for aerospace, medical, industrial and power markets.
markets: Operations and customers across North America, Europe and Asia; grows through bolt-on acquisitions.
rationale: Precision-engineering and aerospace customers fit a technology showcase and B2B hospitality, though brand marketing is limited.

name: Analog Devices
desc: Designs analog, mixed-signal and digital signal processing chips for industrial automation, automotive, communications, healthcare and consumer devices.
markets: Customers worldwide in industrial, automotive and communications; acquired Maxim Integrated in 2021.
rationale: Automotive and sensing technology offers a performance-data showcase, but it is a B2B chipmaker with limited consumer marketing.
changed: Acquired Maxim Integrated in 2021

name: ChangXin Memory Technologies
desc: Chinese maker of DRAM memory chips for PCs, servers and phones, producing in Hefei for China's domestic supply.
markets: Production in Hefei, Anhui; sells mainly to Chinese customers; state and local government funding.
rationale: State-backed, domestically focused chipmaker with no consumer brand and possible export-control sensitivity; weak F1 fit.

name: Emirates Global Aluminium
desc: One of the world's largest aluminium producers, with smelters in Abu Dhabi and Dubai, selling primary aluminium to industrial customers.
markets: Sells to customers in many countries; building a US smelter project in Oklahoma.
rationale: Gulf industrial champion with an Abu Dhabi Grand Prix home-market angle and B2B hospitality value, though it has little consumer marketing.
parent: Mubadala and Investment Corporation of Dubai (equal owners)

name: GlobalFoundries
desc: Contract chipmaker producing specialty and mature-node semiconductors for automotive, IoT, aerospace and mobile customers.
markets: Fabs in New York, Vermont, Germany and Singapore; customers worldwide in automotive, mobile and IoT.
rationale: Automotive chip supply and a technology showcase fit F1, but it is a B2B foundry with limited consumer marketing.

name: Hubbell Incorporated
desc: Makes electrical and utility products, including grid components, wiring devices, connectors and lighting for utility, industrial and commercial customers.
markets: Operations in the US, Canada, Mexico, UK and elsewhere; customers are utilities, industrial and commercial users.
rationale: Grid and electrification focus offers a sustainability tie-in, but it is an industrial B2B brand with limited marketing spend.

name: IonQ
desc: Builds trapped-ion quantum computers and sells access through cloud platforms and direct contracts with enterprises and governments.
markets: Sells via AWS, Azure and Google Cloud; acquisitions added operations in Europe and Asia.
rationale: Quantum computing is a strong technology showcase and B2B hospitality opportunity for enterprise and government buyers.

name: Jabil
desc: Electronics manufacturing services provider building hardware for cloud and AI data centers, healthcare, automotive and communications customers.
markets: Plants across the Americas, Europe and Asia; customers include Apple and data-centre operators.
rationale: Large B2B manufacturer with global customers; hospitality and AI-hardware showcase value but low consumer brand awareness.

name: Lumentum
desc: Designs and makes optical and photonic components, including lasers for 3D sensing and networking parts for AI data centers.
markets: Customers include Apple and cloud and telecom network makers worldwide; growing AI data-centre demand.
rationale: B2B component maker with little consumer profile; technology showcase possible but marketing culture is limited.

name: Rapidus
desc: Japanese semiconductor foundry company aiming to produce 2-nanometer logic chips in Hokkaido, with IBM technology support.
markets: Pre-revenue; building a fab in Chitose, Hokkaido for 2027 production; backed by Japanese firms and government.
rationale: Pre-revenue national-project foundry with no customers yet; weak F1 fit despite a Japan technology story.
changed: Founded in 2022 by Toyota, Sony, NTT, SoftBank, Denso, NEC, Kioxia and MUFG

name: Semiconductor Manufacturing North China
desc: Beijing chip foundry unit of Chinese chipmaker SMIC producing semiconductors, mainly for domestic customers.
markets: Operations in Beijing; customers believed to be mainly in China; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Foundry subsidiary with no consumer brand and no international marketing; very unlikely F1 partner.

name: Solstice Advanced Materials
desc: Specialty materials company making low-global-warming refrigerants, electronic materials, and nuclear and medical packaging materials.
markets: Sells refrigerants and materials worldwide to industrial and electronics customers; operates as an independent company since its 2025 spin-off.
rationale: Sustainability-led refrigerants and materials suit a technology showcase and B2B hospitality, though brand marketing is limited.
changed: Spun off from Honeywell in October 2025

name: TeamSystem
desc: Italian provider of cloud accounting, payroll, e-invoicing and ERP software to small and mid-size businesses and accountants.
markets: Customers in Italy, with operations in Spain, Germany and France; grows through acquisitions.
rationale: Italian software leader with European expansion; Italian Grand Prix hospitality and brand-building possible but F1 use is not obvious.

name: Wesco International
desc: Business-to-business distributor of electrical, industrial and communications products and supply chain services for utilities, data centers and construction customers.
markets: Serves customers in the US, Canada and other countries across utilities, data centers and construction.
rationale: Large B2B distributor with data-centre growth; hospitality value for customers, though it has little consumer brand activity.

name: Grover
desc: Subscription rental service for consumer electronics, offering phones, laptops, wearables and appliances to consumers and businesses.
markets: Operates in Germany, Netherlands, Austria, Spain and the US; consumers and businesses rent devices monthly.
rationale: Consumer-facing circular-economy brand with European growth; a sustainability message could work, but budget is likely limited.

name: UNISOC
desc: Fabless chip designer making 4G and 5G smartphone processors and IoT and TV chips, formerly Spreadtrum and RDA.
markets: Sells to phone makers such as Samsung, Transsion and Realme across Asia, Africa and other emerging markets.
rationale: Chip supplier to emerging-market phone brands; technology showcase possible but export restrictions and low consumer awareness limit fit.

name: Ceconomy
desc: German parent of consumer electronics retailers MediaMarkt and Saturn, operating hundreds of stores and online sales across Europe.
markets: Stores and online shops in Germany and other European countries; JD.com announced a takeover offer in 2025.
rationale: Mass-market European retailer with strong consumer brands and sports sponsorship experience; F1 could drive campaigns across several European markets.
changed: JD.com announced a takeover offer in 2025

name: Hawaiian Electric Industries
desc: Holding company for Hawaiian Electric, the regulated electric utility serving most of Hawaii's population.
markets: Customers in Hawaii only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Regulated single-state utility with no international footprint or consumer marketing culture; weak F1 fit.

name: Videotron
desc: Quebec-based telecommunications and media company offering mobile, internet, television and cable services to consumers and businesses.
markets: Customers in Quebec and, through Freedom Mobile acquired in 2023, other Canadian provinces; no known operations outside Canada.
rationale: Consumer telecom brand in Canada, home of the Montreal Grand Prix; a local sponsorship is plausible but F1 reach is limited.
changed: Acquired Freedom Mobile in 2023

name: Lowe's
desc: Home improvement retailer operating about 1,700 stores in the US and Canada selling appliances, tools, building materials and garden products.
markets: Stores in the US and Canada; no verified expansion outside North America.
rationale: Large consumer retailer already active in US motorsport; United States races could suit it, though international reach is limited.

name: Micron Technology
desc: Produces DRAM memory and NAND flash storage chips for data centers, AI servers, smartphones, PCs and automotive customers.
markets: Fabs in the US, Japan, Taiwan, Singapore and elsewhere; customers worldwide; expanding US and Asian fabs for AI memory.
rationale: AI memory leader with automotive customers; technology showcase and hospitality fit, though it has limited consumer sports marketing.

name: Nidec Corporation
desc: Japanese maker of electric motors, from small precision motors for drives and appliances to automotive traction motors.
markets: Plants and customers across Asia, Europe and the Americas; expanding electric vehicle traction motors and data-centre cooling.
rationale: Electric motor and EV drive technology offers a showcase, but it is a B2B brand with modest consumer marketing.

name: Electrolux
desc: Swedish appliance maker selling refrigerators, ovens, washing machines, dishwashers and vacuum cleaners under Electrolux, AEG and Frigidaire brands.
markets: Sells in about 120 markets across Europe, North America, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Consumer-facing global appliance brand with many markets; F1 could support product launches and retail activation in Europe and the Americas.

name: Command Alkon
desc: Software company supplying dispatch, ticketing, ordering and logistics systems to ready-mixed concrete, aggregates and asphalt producers.
markets: Serves heavy building materials producers; international footprint not verified from the line; no known expansion plans.
rationale: Niche B2B software with a narrow customer base and little consumer profile; weak F1 fit.

name: indie Semiconductor
desc: Fabless chip company selling automotive semiconductors and modules for driver assistance, LiDAR, radar, in-cabin and connectivity systems.
markets: Sells to carmakers and suppliers in the US, Europe and Asia; offices on several continents.
rationale: Automotive technology supplier whose customers overlap with motorsport; a technology showcase fits but it is a small B2B brand.

name: Innoviz Technologies
desc: Israeli maker of automotive LiDAR sensors and perception software that help vehicles detect their surroundings for driver assistance and autonomy.
markets: Supplies carmakers and suppliers in Europe, the US and Asia; customers include Volkswagen group software unit and Mercedes-Benz.
rationale: Automotive sensing technology is a clear technology showcase and B2B hospitality fit with carmaker customers, though its budget is small.

name: SemiDrive
desc: Chinese fabless semiconductor company founded in 2018 making automotive chips for smart cockpits, driver assistance, central computing and vehicle control.
markets: Customers are Chinese carmakers and suppliers; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Domestic automotive chip supplier with low brand awareness outside China; limited F1 fit.

name: Fab 34 JV
desc: Joint venture owning Intel's semiconductor fab in Leixlip, Ireland, where Intel 4 and Intel 3 process chips are manufactured.
markets: Single fab site in Leixlip, County Kildare; output serves Intel's customers; Apollo agreed a stake in 2024.
rationale: Single-asset fab joint venture with no brand of its own; very unlikely to sponsor, though owner Intel is an F1 partner.
changed: Apollo agreed to buy a 49% stake in the JV in 2024
f1: Intel, its majority owner, is a current F1 partner

name: MediaTek
desc: Taiwanese fabless chipmaker designing system-on-chips for smartphones, tablets, smart TVs, Wi-Fi routers, IoT devices and cars.
markets: Dimensity phone chips sold to handset makers worldwide; growing automotive and AI chip business.
rationale: Global consumer-facing chip brand with automotive push; strong fit for technology showcase and handset partner hospitality.

name: Amkor Technology
desc: Provides outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services to fabless firms and chipmakers.
markets: Facilities in Asia, Portugal and the US; customers include Apple and other chip companies worldwide.
rationale: B2B back-end chip supplier with little consumer profile; limited marketing culture and weak F1 fit.

name: Amprion
desc: German electricity transmission system operator running extra-high-voltage grids across western and southwestern Germany.
markets: Operates grid in Germany with cross-border interconnectors; regulated business with no consumer customers.
rationale: Regulated grid operator with no consumer marketing; sponsorship unlikely beyond energy-transition branding.

name: ams OSRAM
desc: Austrian-German photonics and sensor company making LEDs, lasers, optical sensors and automotive lighting for consumer, automotive and industrial customers.
markets: Customers in automotive, mobile and industrial markets in Europe, Asia and the Americas.
rationale: Automotive lighting and sensing give a technology tie-in, and OSRAM carries brand recognition, but marketing is mostly B2B.
changed: Acquired OSRAM in 2020

name: Applied Optoelectronics
desc: Makes optical communications chips, lasers and transceivers for data centers, cable broadband, telecom and fibre-to-the-home networks.
markets: Manufacturing in the US, Taiwan and China; customers include hyperscale data-centre operators, mostly in the US.
rationale: Small B2B component maker with little brand marketing and mostly US customers; weak F1 fit.

name: Asus Global
desc: Singapore-based regional subsidiary of ASUSTeK Computer, the Taiwanese maker of laptops, desktops, motherboards, graphics cards and Republic of Gamers products.
markets: Regional arm of a global PC brand; parent sells worldwide; no entity-specific expansion plans known.
rationale: Parent is a consumer-facing global PC and gaming brand with esports ties; strong technology and fan-engagement fit.

name: Emerson
desc: Automation technology company supplying control systems, valves, measurement instruments, test equipment and industrial software to process and hybrid industries.
markets: Customers in process industries worldwide; owns NI test and measurement business and Copeland stake.
rationale: Industrial automation and data technology suits a showcase and B2B hospitality, though brand marketing is modest.

name: Fortive
desc: Industrial technology company whose units include Fluke test tools, Tektronix, Gordian, Accruent and Provation.
markets: Sells measurement, software and healthcare products worldwide through brands such as Fluke and Tektronix.
rationale: Fluke and Tektronix are known engineering brands, so a technology showcase works; marketing is largely B2B.
changed: Spun off Ralliant in 2025

name: Forward Industries
desc: Designs and makes carry cases and protective solutions for medical devices, tools and consumer electronics.
markets: Design and sourcing business with customers in the US and other markets; details beyond the line not confirmed.
rationale: Small contract design and sourcing firm with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: ITC Holdings
desc: Largest independent US electricity transmission company, operating high-voltage lines across Michigan, Iowa, Minnesota, Illinois and Wisconsin.
markets: Regulated grid operator in several US states only; no international activity.
rationale: Regulated transmission utility with no consumer brand and only US operations; weak F1 fit.

name: PsiQuantum
desc: Developing a fault-tolerant photonic quantum computer using silicon photonics chips manufactured with GlobalFoundries.
markets: Pre-commercial; building sites in the US and Brisbane, Australia; chips made with GlobalFoundries.
rationale: Pre-revenue quantum developer with a technology story, but no product on sale and limited consumer brand marketing.

name: Silicon Box
desc: Singapore-based advanced semiconductor packaging company founded in 2021, offering chiplet integration and panel-level packaging for AI, high-performance computing and mobile.
markets: Factory in Singapore and new plant in Novara, Italy; customers in AI, high-performance computing and mobile.
rationale: Young B2B packaging firm with little brand marketing; technology showcase possible but weak F1 fit.

name: SiTime
desc: Fabless chip company making MEMS-based silicon timing devices, such as oscillators and clock generators, for communications, automotive and consumer markets.
markets: Sells timing chips to customers in the US, Asia and Europe in communications, automotive and consumer markets.
rationale: Precision timing technology has a natural motorsport showcase angle, but it is a small B2B component brand.

name: TTM Technologies
desc: Manufactures printed circuit boards, RF components and assemblies for aerospace and defence, data center, automotive and medical customers.
markets: Plants in the US and Asia; customers in aerospace and defence, data centers and automotive.
rationale: B2B board maker with defence-heavy mix and low brand awareness; weak F1 fit.

name: Tsinghua Unigroup
desc: Chinese semiconductor and technology group whose businesses included UNISOC and memory and chip units; restructured after debt default.
markets: Chip businesses based in China; group restructured after 2021 bankruptcy reorganisation.
rationale: Restructured chip holding with no consumer brand and political sensitivity; unlikely F1 partner.
changed: Entered bankruptcy reorganisation in 2021; control passed to a new investor consortium in 2022

name: OSRAM
desc: Lighting and semiconductor company known for light bulbs and automotive lighting, now part of ams OSRAM.
markets: Automotive lighting and optical chips sold worldwide through ams OSRAM, which acquired it in 2020.
rationale: Well-known consumer lighting brand with automotive tie-in; fit exists, but any deal would sit with parent ams OSRAM.
changed: Acquired by ams in 2020; now operates as ams OSRAM

name: Repay
desc: Provides integrated card and ACH payment processing and merchant acquiring technology to small businesses and verticals such as auto lending.
markets: Customers are US merchants and lenders; no verified international expansion.
rationale: US-only payments processor with B2B focus; F1 hospitality possible but limited international reach.

name: United Nova Technology
desc: Crunchbase describes it as providing electronics system manufacturing for the automotive industry; products and customers are not confirmed.
markets: Based in Shaoxing, Zhejiang; no verified customers, owners or expansion plans.
rationale: Unverified automotive-electronics manufacturer with no known brand activity, customers or owners; weak F1 fit.

name: Applied Materials
desc: Supplies equipment, services and software for manufacturing semiconductors and displays, including deposition, etch and ion implant systems.
markets: Customers are chipmakers and display makers across Asia, North America and Europe.
rationale: Chip equipment leader with strong technology credentials and B2B hospitality value, but little consumer marketing.

name: KnowBe4
desc: Security awareness training and simulated phishing platform used by organisations to train employees against cyber attacks.
markets: Customers in many countries; used by over 70,000 organisations; offices in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Enterprise cybersecurity brand targeting global business buyers; B2B hospitality and security-awareness messaging fit F1 well.
changed: Taken private by Vista Equity Partners in 2023

name: Legrand
desc: French maker of electrical and digital building infrastructure, producing switches, sockets, cable management and data-centre products.
markets: Sells in about 90 countries across Europe, North America and Asia; growing data-centre business.
rationale: Electrification and data-centre products offer a technology showcase, but it sells through installers with limited consumer marketing.

name: OSI Systems
desc: Designs security screening systems under Rapiscan, patient monitoring under Spacelabs, and optoelectronic devices.
markets: Sells screening and monitoring systems to governments, airports and hospitals worldwide.
rationale: Security screening for venues and borders suits B2B hospitality, but government buyers and low consumer profile limit fit.

name: Progress Software
desc: Enterprise software company selling application development, data integration, content management and infrastructure management products.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; grows through acquisitions.
rationale: Enterprise software with global business customers suits B2B hospitality and a technology showcase, though marketing spend is modest.

name: Grupo Energia Bogota
desc: Colombian energy group active in electricity transmission, natural gas transportation and distribution across Colombia and other Latin American countries.
markets: Operations in Colombia, Peru, Brazil and Guatemala; majority owned by Bogota's district government.
rationale: Latin American utility with a regulated, infrastructure business; limited consumer marketing and weak F1 fit.

name: Alliance Laundry Systems
desc: Manufactures commercial laundry equipment, selling washers and dryers under the Speed Queen, UniMac and Huebsch brands.
markets: Sells through distributors in North America and other regions; details of overseas operations are not confirmed.
rationale: B2B appliance maker with niche customers and little motorsport link; modest fit, though Speed Queen has consumer recognition.

name: GoPro
desc: Makes action cameras, mounts and accessories, plus a subscription service for cloud storage and editing.
markets: Sells cameras through retailers and online in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Strong content-led consumer brand with motorsport and adventure audiences; onboard-camera showcase and fan-engagement fit.

name: Advanced Energy Industries
desc: Makes precision power conversion and control systems for semiconductor equipment, industrial, data center, medical and telecom customers.
markets: Sells to equipment makers in North America, Europe and Asia; operations on several continents.
rationale: B2B power electronics supplier with limited consumer awareness; technology showcase possible, but little marketing culture.

name: Cloover
desc: Berlin energy-transition fintech providing embedded financial services and software for solar, storage and heat-pump installers.
markets: Based in Germany; serves installers in European markets; specific countries and expansion plans not confirmed.
rationale: Young B2B fintech with limited budget; sustainability positioning could suit F1, but brand reach is narrow.

name: ContourGlobal
desc: Owns and operates thermal, hydro, wind and solar power plants across Europe, Africa, Latin America and the US.
markets: Plants across Europe, Africa, Latin America and North America; sells power mainly under long-term contracts.
rationale: Power producer with little consumer marketing; energy-transition branding is possible but F1 fit is weak.
changed: Taken private by KKR after a 2022 offer

name: Koch, Inc.
desc: Privately held US conglomerate owning Koch Industries, Flint Hills Resources and other businesses in refining, chemicals, materials and manufacturing.
markets: Businesses operate in about 60 countries across refining, chemicals, fertilizers and manufacturing.
rationale: Large private conglomerate with global operations and B2B hospitality value, though it has little consumer branding to promote.

name: Semtech
desc: Supplies analog and mixed-signal semiconductors, including LoRa wireless chips for IoT and signal integrity products for data centers.
markets: Sells to customers in the Americas, Europe and Asia in communications, industrial and consumer markets.
rationale: B2B chip supplier with a small marketing budget; technology showcase possible but weak F1 fit.

name: Trench Group
desc: Makes high-voltage electrical equipment such as instrument transformers, bushings and air-core reactors for utilities and industry.
markets: Supplies grid equipment to utilities in several regions; details of sales markets are not confirmed.
rationale: Industrial grid-equipment supplier with little consumer profile; weak F1 fit beyond energy-transition branding.
changed: Sold by Siemens Energy to Triton in 2024

name: CCTC
desc: Chinese company that produces and sells electronic components, per Crunchbase; further details are not confirmed.
markets: Based in China; customers and expansion plans not confirmed.
rationale: Unverified component maker with no known brand activity, customers or owners; weak F1 fit.

name: Huahong Group
desc: Shanghai state-owned semiconductor group and parent of Hua Hong Semiconductor, which runs specialty chip foundries.
markets: Foundries in Shanghai and Wuxi; mainly serves Chinese and Asian customers.
rationale: State-owned chip foundry group with no consumer brand; very weak F1 fit.

name: NextNav
desc: Operates a terrestrial positioning network providing 3D location, including floor-level altitude, and timing services for mobile and public safety.
markets: Operates in the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: US-only technology company seeking spectrum approvals; small budget and weak F1 fit.

name: Tata Electronics
desc: Electronics manufacturing arm of the Tata Group making precision components and assembling products such as Apple iPhones in India.
markets: Plants in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka producing for global customers such as Apple; building India's first chip fab.
rationale: Tata Group arm with Indian manufacturing growth; B2B brand but group ties could help, though marketing is group-led.
f1: Group company Tata Communications is a current F1 partner

name: Mirion Technologies
desc: Provides radiation detection, measurement and monitoring products for nuclear power plants, medical, defence and laboratory customers.
markets: Customers in nuclear power, medical and defence in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Niche B2B nuclear-instruments supplier with no consumer marketing and a specialist customer base; weak F1 fit.

name: Sony
desc: Japanese conglomerate with businesses in games (PlayStation), music, pictures, imaging sensors, consumer electronics and financial services.
markets: Sells products and entertainment worldwide; major presence in Japan, the US, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Global consumer brand with gaming, film, camera and sensor businesses; very strong content and technology fit with F1.

name: Haier
desc: Chinese home appliance maker, now part of Haier Smart Home, selling refrigerators, washing machines, air conditioners and other appliances.
markets: Sells under Haier, GE Appliances, Candy and other brands across Asia, North America and Europe.
rationale: Global consumer appliance brand with local sports sponsorship experience; F1 could support European and US campaigns.

name: EnPro Industries
desc: Industrial technology company making sealing products, engineered materials and ultra-clean systems for semiconductor, industrial and life-science markets.
markets: Sells to industrial and semiconductor customers in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B industrial supplier with low consumer awareness and limited marketing spend; weak F1 fit.

name: GTA Semiconductor
desc: Shanghai chip manufacturer operating wafer fabrication for specialty processes, including power, analog and mixed-signal products.
markets: Based in Shanghai; serves electronics and industrial customers, mainly in China; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: B2B foundry with no consumer brand and domestic focus; very weak F1 fit.

name: Yangtze Memory Technologies
desc: Chinese maker of 3D NAND flash memory chips, founded in 2016 and backed by state investment funds.
markets: Production in Wuhan; sells mainly to Chinese customers; subject to US export restrictions.
rationale: State-backed chipmaker under export restrictions with limited consumer marketing; very weak F1 fit.

name: Park Place Technologies
desc: Provides third-party maintenance, monitoring and support services for data center hardware and IT infrastructure.
markets: Service operations in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific for data centre customers.
rationale: Enterprise IT services provider with global customers and B2B hospitality value, though marketing spend is moderate.
f1: Reported owner Carlyle is a current F1 partner (ownership not confirmed here)

name: ESWIN Computing
desc: Beijing chip company developing RISC-V processors, AI chips and related electronics for industrial and automotive customers.
markets: Based in Beijing; customers are mainly in China; no verified overseas expansion.
rationale: Domestic chip developer with no consumer brand and no known international marketing activity; weak F1 fit.

name: Suzhou TA&A Ultra Clean Technology
desc: Chinese maker of ultra-clean gas delivery systems and precision parts for semiconductor equipment and display manufacturing.
markets: Based in Suzhou; customers are chip equipment makers and fabs; international sales not verified.
rationale: B2B parts supplier with no consumer brand and no verified overseas business; very weak F1 fit.

name: Turtle Beach
desc: Designs and sells gaming headsets, controllers, keyboards and mice under the Turtle Beach and ROCCAT brands.
markets: Sells through retailers and online in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Gaming audio brand with esports ties; F1 fan and sim-racing overlap offers a consumer product showcase.

name: findhelp
desc: Social care technology company running a search network that connects people to food, housing and health assistance programs.
markets: Operates in the United States, working with health plans, governments and nonprofits; no verified international operations.
rationale: US social-care platform with a mission focus and limited marketing budget; weak F1 fit.
changed: Renamed from Aunt Bertha

name: Frore Systems
desc: Makes AirJet solid-state active cooling chips for laptops, tablets and other thin electronic devices.
markets: US-based supplier selling to device makers; international sales not verified.
rationale: Cooling technology has a technology showcase angle, but it is a small B2B company with limited marketing budget.

name: Craftsman Automation
desc: Indian engineering company making high-precision powertrain and aluminium components and industrial machinery for vehicle and industrial customers.
markets: Based in Tamil Nadu and listed in India; sells mostly to Indian carmakers and industrial customers.
rationale: Indian component maker with B2B focus; Indian Grand Prix interest is limited and brand marketing is small.

name: Unimicron Technology
desc: Taiwanese maker of printed circuit boards and IC substrates for chip, server and electronics customers.
industry: circuit board and IC substrate maker
markets: Plants in Taiwan, China and Germany; customers include chip and electronics makers worldwide.
rationale: B2B supplier with limited brand marketing; AI-server technology link but weak F1 fit.

name: Rebellions
desc: South Korean AI chip company designing neural processing units and accelerators for data centre AI inference.
markets: Based in Seoul; customers include Korean telecom and cloud firms; wider expansion plans not verified.
rationale: Young AI chip firm with limited consumer brand; technology showcase possible but budget is small.
changed: Merged with SK Telecom's Sapeon in 2024

name: Theon International
desc: Cyprus-registered defence technology company making night vision and thermal imaging equipment for military customers, operating in Greece, Germany and Italy.
industry: night vision and thermal defence optics
markets: Operations in Greece, Germany and Italy; customers are armed forces and defence agencies in many countries.
rationale: Defence-only equipment supplier selling to governments; restricted category and very unlikely F1 partner.

name: WT Microelectronics
desc: Taiwanese electronic components distributor supplying semiconductors and related parts to electronics manufacturers across Asia.
markets: Based in Taipei; distribution mainly across Asia; wider operations not confirmed.
rationale: B2B components distributor with no consumer brand and mainly Asian customers; weak F1 fit.

name: Cambridge Industries USA
desc: US-facing arm of Cambridge Industries Group, a Shanghai maker of optical networking and broadband equipment.
markets: Parent is based in Shanghai and the entity name points to US sales; customers and expansion plans not confirmed.
rationale: B2B network equipment supplier with no consumer brand and unconfirmed customers and ownership details; weak F1 fit.

name: Relativity
